confidence_notes: I based the food and drink anchors on four web searches. They covered aggregated cost-of-living data (CityCost, last updated October 2026, plus Nomad Ranker and Expat Exchange) and 2026 travel guides and menus for General Luna, the main tourist hub. The sources agree on coffee, beer and cocktails. Coffee runs about PHP 120-180 and cappuccinos about USD 2.00-2.65. Beer is about PHP 60-150, and CityCost puts a local draught at about USD 1.29. Cocktails are about PHP 200-320. Mid-range dining varies a lot: CityCost lists USD 19.60 for two, while 2026 guides say PHP 500-1,000 per person in General Luna. I set the mid-range meal toward the tourist-area level. I found no direct wine-by-the-glass prices, so the wine anchor is estimated from its usual relationship to beer and cocktail prices, with imported wine priced at a premium. The accommodation anchors are my own estimates from general knowledge. I did not search or check any live listings for them. July is not the peak season, but Siargao's prices are high for the Philippines and change quickly, so the accommodation figures are the least certain. The FX observation is the RBA 4.00pm AUD/USD rate for 18 November 2026, the latest one my search found.
comparable_city_reasoning: Prices are calibrated to a tourist-oriented Philippine island. Siargao sits above Manila and Cebu for drinks and Western-style dining, and is broadly similar to El Nido and Boracay's budget-to-mid tiers. CityCost puts Siargao's overall costs about 36% below Makati and about 38% below Phuket.
